output:
I found four households (HH-0928, HH-0592, HH-4821, HH-0586) whose billing groups go against a signed householding agreement. The pattern is the same in all four.

Each household has three accounts: a joint account, one spouse's IRA, and an adult child's individual account. In each, all three account holders signed a householding letter saying all three accounts "are billed together as one group from the next billing cycle." The portfolio system still bills them as two groups. The parents' two accounts are in one group and the child's account is in a separate group on its own. Both groups were last changed in 2021, when the child's own advisory agreement was signed. That is before each householding letter, so the letters were never put into billing.

| Household | Agreement (signed) | Billing groups that keep the accounts apart | Groups last changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0928 (Jablonski) | AGR-0928-3 (2024-03-05) | BG-0928-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-0928-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-01 |
| HH-0592 (Haddad) | AGR-0592-3 (2023-10-20) | BG-0592-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-0592-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-01 |
| HH-4821 (Okafor-Lind) | AGR-4821-3 (2024-11-18) | BG-4821-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-4821-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-14 |
| HH-0586 (Quarshie) | AGR-0586-3 (2024-06-07) | BG-0586-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-0586-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-01 |

**What I checked**
- **Which households have one:** I searched every household's CRM file. These are the only four with a householding agreement.
- **The agreements stand:** each was signed and on file well before 15 April 2026. Nothing later in the CRM cancels or changes it; each household's last note is an October 2025 annual review recording "No changes requested."
- **The accounts are still open:** all three accounts in each household are open at the custodian as of 15 April 2026.
- **No other explanation:** none of the four has a separate agreement, an approved exception or a later correction.

**Not checked**
- I didn't work out how much each household was overbilled. All four use the standard tiered fee schedule FS-STD, so billing the child's account separately probably costs more than billing all three together. The amount would need the quarter-end values.
- HH-7350's advisory agreement says Aiko Sato "has not agreed to household billing." That's the opposite problem, and it doesn't involve a householding agreement, so I didn't look into it.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households are billed in groups that a signed householding agreement contradicts?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households are, "none_found" if none is, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household that is, each as {"household_id": ..., "agreement_id": the householding agreement, "billing_group_ids": the billing groups that hold its accounts apart, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
